entities.summary: Dmitry Mikhaylovich Pozharsky was a Russian prince known for his military leadership during the Polish–Russian War from 1611 to 1612. Pozharsky formed the Second Volunteer Army with Kuzma Minin in Nizhny Novgorod against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth's occupation of Russia during the Time of Troubles, resulting in Polish withdrawal after Russian victory at the Battle of Moscow in 1612. Pozharsky received the unprecedented title of Saviour of the Fatherland from Mikhail I of Russia, becoming a folk hero in Russian culture and honored in the Monument to Minin and Pozharsky in Moscow's Red Square.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pozharsky's leadership in the Second Volunteer Army led to the Polish withdrawal from Russia after the Battle of Moscow in 1612, ending the Time of Troubles and securing Russian independence. This victory had significant regional implications, marking a turning point in Russian history.
